title: Over-Fragmented Aggregates (Direct Object Reference Misuse)
pattern: Placing a direct object reference to a foreign Aggregate Root inside another Aggregate, merging their consistency boundaries.
why_bad: Implies that the foreign aggregate (`Customer`) is part of the referencing aggregate's (`Order`) consistency boundary. Mutating `customer` through `Order` violates the invariant that changes to an aggregate must be checked only by its own root. It also forces the persistence layer to load the entire `Customer` record inside the `Order` transaction, slowing throughput.
detection: Look for struct fields representing foreign Aggregate Roots instead of referencing them strictly via their unique identifiers.
counterexample: Transient domain representations in memory for read-only view models (DTOs) where transactional consistency is not active.
source: *Vaughn Vernon - Implementing Domain-Driven Design (2013)*, Chapter 10, "Aggregates" (Rule: Reference Other Aggregates by Identity, p. 359).
